call_points.text: FY27 capex outflow about ₹800 Cr, including ₹600-700 Cr for battery projects and ₹100 Cr for Neogen.
Pakhajan electrolyte commercial manufacturing targeted H1FY27; electrolyte salts H2FY27.
One domestic giga customer is expanding from 1 GWh to 5 GWh in H1; Neogen is its only source.
Three US electrolyte makers completed site audits; commercial supplies expected by July-August 2026.
Q4 EBITDA margin held at 17.8% despite expansion overheads and Dahej toll-manufacturing costs.
Insurance claims: ₹140 Cr received cumulatively plus ₹7 Cr salvage; net claim receivable ₹203 Cr.

industry: Commodities > Chemicals > Chemicals & Petrochemicals > Specialty Chemicals

operating_notes.text: Bromine derivatives were about 40-45% of Organic Chemicals revenue, advanced intermediates about 30%, and organolithium plus lithium the balance.
Organolithium capacity was raised 2.5x to 300 MT/year; management targets 80-90% utilisation this year.
Total salt plus additive capacity is 5,500 MT (about 4,000 MT salts, 1,500 MT additives), plus a new 500 MT intermediate facility.
Organo-lithium capacity of 300 tonnes per annum hit full utilisation in Q1FY27, up 2.5x from 120 tonnes per annum.
Battery chemicals capacity is designed for 40 GWh of salts and 30 GWh of electrolyte, with FY29 revenue potential of ₹2,400–2,900 Cr.
Base-business working capital cycle is about 140–160 days, targeted at 140 days by FY28; battery business targeted at 90 days.

timeline.summary: On its 18 May 2026 Q4FY26 call, Neogen guided FY27 standalone revenue to ₹875-950 Cr (cut from ₹950-1,000 Cr) and battery chemicals above ₹300 Cr, with Dahej Phase 1 at ₹428 Cr by February 2027 and Pakhajan Phase 2 at ₹1,367 Cr by March 2027.

On its 27 July 2026 Q1FY27 call, Neogen raised FY27 base-business revenue guidance to ₹950–1,050 Cr after 34% revenue growth, kept battery chemicals at ₹300 Cr and said the board approved a ₹600 Cr QIP.

watchlist.target: above ₹300 Cr for FY27, mostly H2

watchlist.response: Management cited lower average lithium prices during the year but said it would need a closer look before answering; volumes described as broadly stable.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the reason behind the continuous drag in Inorganic Chemicals ex-Neogen Ionics

watchlist.response: Management said the repayment schedule has been extended to match the project delay, the extra capex was funded by promoter and JV equity, and it would raise money if needed.
watchlist.text: Analyst flagged a potential liquidity issue if capacity ramp-up is delayed

watchlist.response: Management said ROCE remains 18-20% after the revised capex, with 20% the base target on the salt side.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the return on the ₹250 Cr+ higher battery project capex versus the earlier 18% ROCE expectation
Shareholder and regulatory approvals for the ₹600 Cr QIP

watchlist.response: Management said there was some benefit from older inventory but that quantifying it was 'very difficult'
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how much of the Q1 gross-margin gain came from selling older inventory

watchlist.response: Management said it cannot promise consistently positive cash flows while the company is growing, and pointed to FY29 as the year of full utilisation and better conversion
